Buying Land in Northern Colorado

Wells, Septic Systems, Zoning, Utilities, and What You Need to Know

Water Wells in Colorado

Most rural properties in Colorado rely on private wells. Well usage rights are tied to property size and permit type.

  • Under 35 acres: Likely a household-use only permit (indoor use only).
  • 35+ acres: May qualify for a domestic well (indoor, livestock, and limited irrigation).

Learn more at the Colorado Division of Water Resources

Septic Systems

Most homes on land have private septic systems. It's essential to know local requirements and get inspections.

  • Larimer County: Requires a Transfer of Title inspection and cleanout.
  • Weld County: Inspection must be requested — not automatic.

Ask for inspection reports and last pump dates when buying.

Zoning, Setbacks & Property Use

Zoning defines how you can use your land. Setbacks determine where you can build.

  • Common Zoning Types: Residential, Agricultural, and Open (in Larimer)
  • Open Zoning: Often found in Larimer County; designed to preserve natural areas with limited development

Larimer Zoning Info | Weld Zoning Info

Survey vs ILC

An ILC (Improvement Location Certificate) shows boundaries and structures. A full land survey offers exact legal property lines.

  • Use ILCs for basic purchases or refinancing
  • Get a full survey before fencing, building, or resolving boundary issues

Utilities & Infrastructure

Rural land may require significant setup for utilities.

  • Water Taps: Can exceed $30,000–$90,000 depending on district
  • Electric: Power poles cost $1,200–$5,000 each; spaced 125–300 ft apart
  • Internet: May require satellite or long-range wireless solutions

Financing Land

Land loans are different from home loans. Down payments range from 15%–50% depending on:

  • Raw vs improved land
  • Lender requirements
  • Whether utilities or access exist

Bonus: If you're buying land with a home already on it, ask about USDA Loans — they offer 0% down in eligible rural areas! Check USDA Eligibility Map

FAQs

What is the 35-acre rule for wells?

Properties over 35 acres may qualify for a domestic well that allows outdoor watering. Under 35 acres is usually restricted to indoor use only.

Do I need a land survey or just an ILC?

ILC is fine for financing. Surveys are better for legal boundaries and building.

Can I build a shop or barn?

Most likely — but it depends on your zoning and local setback requirements. Check county rules.

How much does a septic system cost?

Installations run $10,000–$25,000+. Inspection and pumping usually cost $300–$600.

Can I finance land like a home?

Yes, but land loans often require higher down payments and different terms. Talk to a land-friendly lender. You may qualify for USDA loans if you're purchasing land with a home in designated areas — with 0% down! Check USDA eligibility here.
